name: iHEL Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: iHEL's top singles belt: a four-way elimination on 16 August 2000, staged as a double-stakes match with the Television title in the same ring, cost Big_Daddy the Heavyweight belt and handed it to British_Kid in the same night.

name: iHEL Television Championship
epitaph: iHEL's television belt changed hands in the very match that cost its own outgoing Heavyweight Champion his title: a four-way elimination on 16 August 2000 sent Jay_Biess's TV reign to Big_Daddy, the same man just dethroned as Heavyweight Champion.

name: iHEL Pitfighter Championship
epitaph: A hardcore belt decided inside a local convenience store: Drater walked out of a four-way "Jiffy Store Brawl" on 16 August 2000 as the new Pitfighter Champion, no prior holder named in the surviving record.

name: iTFA Television Championship
epitaph: Arrow lost the iTFA Television title to Vapor in a three-way on 15 August 2000, only for the belt to sit vacant again within two days as Vapor chased the People's Championship instead — the next card's own preview reports the vacancy without a captured replacement match.

name: iTFA Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Freezer and Pimp_man won the iTFA Tag Team Championship on 15 August 2000, billed by the fed's own report as becoming the "OFFICIAL" champions — language that reads as the title's own first sanctioned decision rather than a change of hands.

name: UIWA World-Class Tag Team Championship
epitaph: High Intelligence (Pennance and Jordanzombie) lost the World-Class Tag Team Championship to Murder Inc. (Sinacle and Marley) under hardcore rules at Stormfront, 11 August 2000.

name: UIWA Universal Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: Sinacle upset four-time, seven-month champion Whipple_jr for the Universal Heavyweight Championship at Stormfront on 11 August 2000 — one reign inside a much longer Whipple_jr lineage the surviving record never fully recovers.

name: iQFWC United States Championship
epitaph: Deth dethroned Mad_hatter for the iQFWC United States Championship at Thursday Terror, 20 January 2001, winning 6-2.

name: iQFWC Blood and Guts Championship
epitaph: Mikey_ripper became the new iQFWC Blood and Guts Champion at Thursday Terror, 20 January 2001, judged on rewrite quality after Wendell failed to make the card and Randy came up short.

name: iQFWC Contenders Championship
epitaph: An unusual belt awarded inside its own contendership match: Hex beat Lordy on points, 15-13, in a Hell in a Cell contenders final at Thursday Terror, 20 January 2001, to "take home the contenders Title."

name: iQFWC World Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Last Rites (Cripler and Deth), who won the belts from Psychotic Tendancies at a show the surviving record doesn't capture, turned back a challenge from Black Magic (Voodoo_death and Voodoo_lord) at Thursday Terror, 20 January 2001.

name: iMWA World Championship
epitaph: A title that moved three times across one week in the surviving record: Amundson beat a seven-time champion, Bolt, for the belt; Mr Arse took it from Amundson on the Friday of the two-night Road to CWZ card; and the very next night Mr Arse lost a separate Loser Leaves iMWA match and left the belt vacant on his way out the door to the CWZ.

name: iMWA Tag Team Championship
epitaph: The_Crew "regained" the iMWA Tag Team Championship from Sickness 2K in a no-holds-barred cage match on the Friday of Road to CWZ, 29 September 2000 — Sickness 2K splitting up in the match's own aftermath.

name: iMWA Holy Scripture Championship
epitaph: A one-off tournament belt: Damion won a final billed only as "winner of match one vs winner of match two" to become the new Holy Scripture Champion on the Saturday of Road to CWZ, 30 September 2000 — his own final opponent unnamed in the surviving text.

name: iUIWA Showstoppa Championship
epitaph: Slobberknock beat Anarky to regain the Showstoppa title, only for the belt to go vacant in the same report on his own promotion out of the iUIWA — undated in the source itself, bounded by a 4 March 2000 Wayback capture.

name: iUIWA Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: Carrion became the iUIWA Heavyweight title holder by beating Way, reported in the same undated post as the Showstoppa change and bounded the same way by a 4 March 2000 Wayback capture.

name: iUWA Underdogg Championship
epitaph: Tomango was billed as the iUWA's reigning Underdogg Champion in the fed's own 16 August 2000 column naming every current titleholder, no captured match establishing when the reign began.

name: iUWA SkullCrusher Championship
epitaph: Sabit was billed as the iUWA's reigning SkullCrusher Champion in the fed's own 16 August 2000 column, which frames the belt as "more of a tradition" than an ordinary championship.

name: iUWA Television Championship
epitaph: Zabingu was billed as the iUWA's reigning Television Champion in the fed's own 16 August 2000 column naming every current titleholder.

name: iUWA World Championship
epitaph: Slammin Stu was billed as the iUWA's reigning World Champion in the fed's own 16 August 2000 column; a later preview (30 August) frames a World title match between two other slammers without naming a champion, a possible untracked change the surviving record doesn't resolve.

name: CWO United States Championship
epitaph: Wholyevil billed himself, in his own Hammerlock News interview, as the reigning CWO United States Champion — the interview is undated in the source and names no opponent or show.

name: CCWe Underdawg Championship
epitaph: Massacre_sr was stripped of the CCWe Underdawg Championship on 19 January 2001 for violating the fed's own jobbing and padding policies, the vacancy turning a scheduled Triple Threat into a Fatal 4 Way whose own result the surviving record doesn't capture.

name: iGWF World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: Hak dethroned Dysturbed for the iGWF World Heavyweight Championship with help from stablemate TripleXXX, reported only in the winner's own newly-crowned-champion interview on 16 August 2000, no date or show captured beyond it.

name: CRF World Championship
epitaph: Con_victor, promoted up from the iIWF, was billed as the reigning CRF World Champion defending against Juggernaut and Wheelie on the CRF's own 3 February 2001 return card, posted as CyberSlam's own shutdown crisis threatened to end the game.

name: CRF Can-Am Championship
epitaph: Mr Peak was billed as the reigning CRF Can-Am Champion on the fed's own 3 February 2001 return card, defending against Hell Spawn and Triple C.

name: CRF Enforcer Championship
epitaph: Manowar was billed as the reigning CRF Enforcer Champion on the fed's own 3 February 2001 return card, a hardcore defense against The Monk, Pagan, Carnage and Batman.

name: CRF Television Championship
epitaph: El Jobre was billed as the reigning CRF Television Champion on the fed's own 3 February 2001 return card, defending against The_g_a_m_e and Agent_orange.

name: CRF Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Manowar and Mr Peak, billed together as "Over & Out," were the reigning CRF Tag Team Champions on the fed's own 3 February 2001 return card, defending against Myth Inc. and the CRF Gods.

name: CRF Rapid Fire Championship
epitaph: Triple C was billed as the reigning CRF Rapid Fire Champion on the fed's own 3 February 2001 return card, defending against Freebird and Baretta.
